stem: Rohan's teacher asks the class: "Which of these objects is a member of the Solar System, and shines only because it reflects sunlight?"

options.text: The Pole Star, because it looks bright in the night sky
The Moon, because it reflects light from the Sun
A comet, because it makes its own light like the Sun
Sirius, because it is the brightest star we can see

teacher.key_rationale: The Moon belongs to the Solar System and shines by reflecting sunlight, not by producing its own light. Stars like the Pole Star and Sirius produce their own light and are not members of the Solar System; a comet is a member but does not produce its own light.
